for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$."] [:db/add "89e0ec45-c6c5-510c-8d5d-815a56ed5603" :question/worked-solution "The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & -3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=1 \\ y &=0-(1)(1) \\ &=-1 \\ x &=-3-(-2)(-1) \\ &\quad -(-1)(1) \\ &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-4,-1,1\right)
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right]

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=1 \\ y &=0-(1)(1) \\ &=-1 \\ x &=-3-(-2)(-1) \\ &\quad -(-1)(1) \\ &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-4,-1,1\right)
$$
